newsitem.title: CANADA: Viridian climbs on Agrium merger news.
newsitem.headline: Viridian climbs on Agrium merger news.

text.p: Shares of fertilizer firm Viridian Inc jumped in heavy trade on Monday after it an Agrium Inc said they agreed to a merger deal that would create an operation with a market capitalization of more than C$2.5 billion.
Viridian, formerly the fertilizer arm of Sherritt Inc, climbed 1.50 to 18 on volume of 3.12 million shares. Agrium fell 0.70 to 18.20 on 377,300 shares.
The firms said on Sunday they agreed to a stock swap in whcih Viridian shareholders would receive 0.975 Agrium shares for each Viridian share.

Industry players had speculated that Viridian was headed for a deal since Sherritt was split earlier this year into Sherritt International Corp, the vehicle for the company's Cuban energy and mining operations, and Viridian, its Alberta-based fertilizer business.
The companies said this year's estimated cash balance for the combined entity was expected to be about C$400 million.
They said Agrium intended to use a portion of the war chest to buy back about 10 percent of the merged firm's outstanding shares after the deal's completion.
Based on Monday's trading prices, the value of the deal would be about C$1.33 billion.

"The merger further secures our position as a leader in the production and marketing of nitrogen and phosphate fertilizers by enhancing our ability to better serve our customers through the more efficient use of the combined facilities," Agrium chief executive John Van Brunt said in a statement.
"This, in turn, is complemented by our major presence in the potash and agricultural retail businesses."
